hints: Notice the crop is successfully growing, so water must be moving INTO the root hair cells from the soil at -40 KPa. Which way must water flow?
Remember water always moves by osmosis from higher (less negative) to lower (more negative) water potential. What must the root hair cell sap be compared to -40 KPa for this to happen?
walkthrough:
**Spot what is happening**

Great start, let's read the story. The maize is growing well, so its roots must be absorbing water from the soil.

That means net movement is: soil solution -> root hair cell.

**Apply the water potential rule**

Water always moves down a water potential gradient, from higher $\Psi$ (less negative, closer to zero) to lower $\Psi$ (more negative).

$$ \text{water moves: higher } \Psi \rightarrow \text{ lower } \Psi $$

**Pick the only possible value**

Soil $\Psi = -40 \text{ KPa}$. For water to enter, the cell sap must be more negative than this.

Only $-60 \text{ KPa}$ is lower than $-40 \text{ KPa}$, so that must be the answer.

options.A: Correct. -60 KPa is more negative (lower) than soil at -40 KPa, so water moves by osmosis into the root hair cell down the gradient.
options.B: No net movement would occur. If both are -40 KPa there is no water potential gradient, so no uptake for growth.
options.C: This is higher than the soil. Water would move out of the root into the soil, which would dehydrate and wilt the plant.
options.D: Pure water at 0 KPa is much higher than soil. Water would leave the root very rapidly, the opposite of absorption.
